scientific_impact_assessment.phase_g_intent: Verify whether 360p proxy compression explains Baseline A failure
rationale: Median Baseline A frame errors are 94f (takeoff), 89f (apex), 85f (water_contact) — equivalent to 1.4–3.1 seconds at 30–60fps.
360p compression artifacts could introduce at most 2–5 frames of uncertainty, three orders of magnitude smaller than observed errors.
The dominant failure modes (EARLY_TRIGGER, TRAJECTORY_COLLAPSE, WATER_CONTACT_RUNAWAY) are structural algorithmic failures, not quality-sensitive detection misses.
Even with perfect original quality, the MOG2+centroid architecture would produce the same systematic errors.
Therefore: proxy quality is NOT a plausible cause of Baseline A failure. Phase G would be uninformative even if originals were available.
scientific_impact_assessment.conclusion: Phase G result is predictable without running: no material difference expected between proxy and original Baseline A predictions.
